idea_headline: Everything is a game, so make it feel like one.
idea: Arcade is the cabinet with the lights on: a near-white ground with a faint checker, pixel-black ink, and the NES primaries (red, blue, yellow, with magenta and cyan for the power-ups). Status is an HP bar that goes green, yellow, red in blocks. Lives are hearts, points are coins, hints blink, wins get a ribbon. Night is the CRT: black glass, scanlines, the colours lifted to neon.
use_for: Game and launch pages, leaderboards and trackers, hackathons, playful dashboards, teaching material for kids and anyone else, anything that gets better with a score.
avoid_when: Serious, institutional or long-reading subjects; dense data; anything where a pixel heart would read as a joke at the reader's expense.
principles_headline: Snap to the pixel. Keep score. Celebrate.
principles: Every sprite, frame and shadow is a multiple of 4px. Nothing is anti-aliased: SVG uses crispEdges, corners are stepped with box-shadow, never rounded.
Green blocks for full, yellow for half, red for low, with a glyph or a word. No other colour carries state; magenta and cyan are power-ups.
Points are coins, lives are hearts.
Small counts with a goal are a row of coins; chances left are hearts. Three coins is a win and gets a ribbon.
Cabinet red for the primary action, hearts and the player sprite. Blue is player two: the second fill, the first chart series.
Press Start 2P for three-word headlines, the HUD and tags only. Pixelify Sans carries reading; VT323 carries the numbers.
voice: Short imperatives in caps where the HUD speaks: INSERT COIN, PRESS START, LEVEL UP, GAME OVER.
Scores are zero-padded: 004120. Multipliers get an exclamation mark: ×3 COMBO!
Reading text is plain, friendly and a little cheeky; the pixel voice is for the HUD, not the paragraph.
Dialogue boxes speak like an NPC: one sentence, then ▼.
colour_headline: Near-white, pixel ink, the NES primaries, an HP bar.
colour_note: Day is the cabinet: a near-white ground with a faint checker, ink pixels, red primary, blue for player two, yellow coins, magenta and cyan power-ups. Night is the CRT: black glass with 4px scanlines and every colour lifted to neon. Green, yellow and red carry status in blocks; nothing else does.
chart_note: Blue leads so bars never impersonate the HP bar; red is the comparison; yellow the highlight for the top score. Magenta and cyan come last.
type_headline: Press Start 2P shouts, Pixelify plays, VT323 counts.
type_note: Press Start 2P only for headlines of three words, HUD labels and tags, never above 44px. Pixelify Sans at 18px carries all reading and, bold italic, the one celebratory word. VT323 carries scores and dialogue at 22px and up.
space: The unit. Everything snaps to it.
Control padding-x; the checker size; one HP block.
Between panels, so pixel shadows never touch.
edges: A 4px frame drawn with four box-shadows (top, bottom, left, right) so the corners step: the pixel-rounded border. Buttons, tags, the dialogue box.
Panels and fields take a plain 4px ink border.
The pixel edge plus two more shadows at 8px: a hard stepped drop. Buttons and the active panel; press removes it.
depth: The stepped pixel shadow only. No blur, ever.
Night only: a 4px repeating line at 5% over the whole page, like glass.
The ground texture: 16px squares in sunk. Faint by day, nearly invisible by night.
motion: PRESS START and the dialogue ▼ blink at 1Hz with step timing. Reduced motion shows them steady.
Buttons jump 4px into their shadow on press. No easing: steps(1).
Numbers count up in 60ms ticks on first paint (the kit animate-fade-in on the numeral is the fallback).
Panels use the kit reveal-up; sprites may use animate-float, one per page, as the idle bob.
A ribbon slides in from the left in 120ms, steps(4). It stays.

hand.headline: Eight-pixel cells, four-pixel ink, no curves.
hand.note: Arcade draws like a sprite sheet: every shape snaps to an 8px cell, the ink is a 4px square-capped stroke, fills are flat red and blue, and the SVG is rendered with crispEdges so nothing is smoothed. Any subject can be a sprite; keep it under sixteen cells wide so it reads at any size.
rules: 8px cells. Coordinates and sizes snap; a shape narrower than one cell does not exist.
4px ink, square caps, square joins, crispEdges.
Flat red for the player part, blue for player two, blue-soft for the quiet part, sunk for empty.
None inside a drawing; the panel around it carries the stepped shadow.
Press Start 2P at 10px for labels; VT323 for the one number.
Sprites move in 4px steps; one may bob with animate-float.

dos: Snap everything to 4px; crisp edges only.
Status in HP blocks: green, yellow, red, with a glyph.
Yellow for the one highlighted figure; a ribbon for the win.
Press Start 2P for three-word headlines and the HUD; Pixelify for reading.
donts: No anti-aliased shapes, no rounded corners, no blur.
No magenta or cyan as status.
No Press Start 2P paragraphs or anything above 44px.
binding_losses: The pixel edge and stepped shadow, the scanlines, the checker ground, the HP blocks, the coins, hearts and the dialogue box have no contract slot; they are the --ds-pixel-edge and --ds-pixel-shadow properties and the ar-* classes, plus inline SVG with crispEdges. The ink border rides the border token so kit frames are ink.
footer: Cabinet first, CRT second. Fonts: Press Start 2P 400, Pixelify Sans 400/500/700, VT323 400, all Google-hosted.

tpl.slide_sub: A playthrough in six slides: the score, the coins, the blocks, and where the trouble is.
tpl.slide_body: Nine of thirteen blocks are green. Below half they turn yellow; below a quarter, red, and that is where you lose a life.
tpl.ed_headline: How the Foundry door really opens
tpl.ed_deck: Three coins, one shopkeeper, and the red blocks everyone hits on the first try. A walk through level three, with the scores to prove it.
tpl.ed_body: The Foundry starts you with two hearts and no coins. The first coin is free; the second is behind the moving platform; the third is where the shopkeeper stands, and he wants a word before you take it. Most runs end on the red blocks between the second coin and the third, which is the point of the level: the door is easy, the walk to it is not.
steps: One hundred players start the level. Each cell is a player; red means still playing, blue means through the door.
Sixty are through, twenty-five are stuck on the platform, fifteen have gone back to the shop. The level is doing its job.
tpl.landing_sub: A page that keeps score: coins for progress, hearts for chances, an HP bar for anything with a threshold, and a ribbon when you win.
features: Every count is a number you can beat. Zero-padded, in VT323, with a high score beside it.
Goals are small and visible: a row of coins that fill as you go.
Status is green, yellow or red blocks with a glyph. You always know where the trouble is.
